about.text: Marion County is one of three counties in Indiana (along with St. Joseph County and Lake County) in which the governor appoints judges to serve on the superior court, subject to retention elections—a method of judicial selection referred to as the “Missouri Plan.” Relying on demographic data, Cheston Roberts alleged that the selective implementation of the Missouri Plan in only these three counties violated § 2 of the Voting Rights Act and the Constitution.

caseName: Cheston Roberts v. State of Indiana, et al
